title: The Cowherd and the Weaver Girl
place: Earth, the heavens, and the Silver River
sourceAuthor: Richard Wilhelm; translated by Frederick H. Martens
note: A new, child-oriented adaptation of “The Herd Boy and the Weaving Maiden.” The coercive clothing episode in the historical source is omitted; the lovers meet by mutual choice.

rights.basis: The 1921 source edition is identified as public domain in the United States by Project Gutenberg.

artLabel: A cowherd and celestial weaver meet on a bridge of magpies across the starry Milky Way.

pageArt.alt: The Queen Mother draws the shining Silver River between Niulang and Zhinü.
Niulang and Zhinü approach each other across a bridge formed by magpies over the Milky Way.

scenes: Niulang was a lonely cowherd whose old ox was his truest companion. High above, Zhinü wove glowing clouds beside the heavenly loom.
One summer evening, Zhinü came down to the earthly fields. She and Niulang met beneath the stars, and in time chose to make a home together.
But the ruler of heaven commanded Zhinü back to her loom. With one sweep of a hairpin, the Queen Mother drew a shining river across the sky between them.
Niulang stood on one bank of the Milky Way and Zhinü on the other. Their sorrow moved every magpie in the world.
On the seventh night of the seventh month, the birds formed a bridge with their wings. The two crossed the Silver River and met again.
Look up on a clear summer night: the stars Altair and Vega still wait on opposite shores.
